checks: stored snapshot hashes independently verified against their pages

methodology: Live performance comparison uses the original uninstrumented node and CLI binaries, same host, 105 identical gameplay inputs per version; optimized run followed by a fresh baseline run. Each ran alone without other benchmarks or compilation in progress.

Baseline is the previous 10 MiB/6 MiB-zone implementation with urllib reconnects, serial reads and full-frame preflight. Its node used the detected 9 workers. Optimized uses 6 MiB guest memory, 3 MiB zone, 4 MiB arena, 64000-byte snapshot entries, stored page hashes, batched frame reads, persistent HTTP and 2 workers.
Every tick is one signed native pubkey-wallet transaction committed in one block. Frames are read from committed contract storage. Browser drawing/display latency is excluded.

HTTP means include stalls. Aggregate FPS is 1000 / mean HTTP milliseconds. Reciprocal median latency is not the aggregate framerate. Historical 19 FPS was a shorter earlier sample; fresh baseline is 17.14 FPS.
Comparisons use the same 20 forward inputs then 85 right-turn inputs. Initial and final committed pixel/palette buffers match, excluding transport metadata.

Standalone 1050-tick input sequence and 152 recorded frames match the prior default. Independent verification hashes the stored snapshot pages after initialization and after gameplay, outside measured tick spans.

The 2 MiB zone variant failed with Z_Malloc out of memory; 3 MiB passed. One worker was slower (43.70 ms mean HTTP, 22.88 FPS) than two and is not the default. Results concern this E1M1 internal demo, not arbitrary levels or long sessions.
Intermediate pages64 runs overlapped a standalone validation workload and are excluded from the primary performance comparison.

Temporary profiling node adds clock reads and INFO probes; its measurements are explanatory and separate from the uninstrumented live performance comparison. Syscall spans include coroutine suspension. Block spans use millisecond event-service timestamps; otherBlockMs is a per-sample residual, and separate medians do not add exactly.
No cross-block prepared-code caching changes, protocol ceiling changes, or off-chain game simulation.
tradeoff: Larger snapshot entries reduce storage RPC count but increase changed bytes written: median 392528 to 579056 bytes/tick. Hash table and pages commit atomically. Snapshot format version is now 2; redeploy with a fresh data directory and max_bytestring_len=64000.
